conclusion: We introduced Spectral-Spatial Interpretation (SSI), which explains predictions of multi-channel image models at the level of joint position-channel players [math] . SSI fixes the observed surrounding context and allocates each position’s contribution among its channels via the Shapley value, producing a full attribution matrix whose channel aggregation exactly recovers the position-level contextual contrast. Across CUB-200, EuroSAT, and HLS Burn Scar, SSI improves joint faithfulness, spectral hit rates, and channel deletion over dense, flat, and rank-1 baselines, and outperforms MC-Owen on HLS Burn Scar with roughly [math] of its evaluation budget.
